title: US ‘highly likely’ to lose measles elimination status this fall, analysis warns | CIDRAP
snippet:
Declining vaccination coverage appears to be a key factor in the measles resurgence. Coverage among kindergarteners in the 2024–25 school year was below the 95% needed to maintain herd immunity against measles. 

The situation mirrors a broader global trend. Canada lost its measles elimination status in late 2025, and several European countries, including Spain and the United Kingdom, have lost their status amid rising case counts. [...] > Given the current epidemiological context, it appears highly likely that the USA will lose its measles elimination status in 2026.

While the current analysis relies on older elimination criteria (the upcoming status review might use updated measures), the much larger number of cases in 2025 and 2026 than in 2011 suggests that the country’s elimination status is in jeopardy. [...] Measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, meaning there was no continuous transmission for at least 12 months. The milestone was achieved following years of nationwide vaccination efforts, including the adoption of a two-dose measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) immunization schedule.

The current resurgence threatens that status. With 2,288 confirmed cases in 2025 and 1,814 confirmed cases as of last week, the country is experiencing its largest measles outbreak in decades.

title: US adds 53 more measles cases to its 2026 total
snippet:
Among the current measles hotspots is Pennsylvania, which has reported 31 new cases over the past seven days and now has 167 cases for the year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health. Officials in neighboring Ohio yesterday confirmed four new cases in unvaccinated individuals in Ashtabula and Tuscarawas counties. It’s Ohio’s third measles outbreak this year. [...] # US adds 53 more measles cases to its 2026 total

News brief

Chris Dall, MA

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) confirmed 53 new US measles cases this week, bringing the total for the year to 2,371 cases. [...] The number of US measles cases as of July 30 has already surpassed the 2,289 reported for all of 2025. Both figures represent the highest annual number of cases in the nation since 1991. The United States was declared measles-free in 2000 but appears likely to lose its measles elimination status later this year, when officials with the Pan American Health Organization review transmission data.

title: US measles cases reach 35-year high, for second record-breaking year in a row
snippet:
The measles outbreak in South Carolina started in October, contributing to what was a record-breaking — and deadly — year for measles in the US. Nearly 2,300 measles cases were reported last year, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — ​about 12 times more than the annual average since measles was declared eliminated in the US and the worst year in more than three decades. [...] Measles has continued its historic resurgence in the United States this year, with a second record-breaking year in a row. Just over halfway through 2026, the country has recorded more cases than in any other year since 1991 – surpassing a grim milestone that was just topped last year.

The disease was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, but more cases have been recorded in the past 18 months than there have been in the previous 25 years combined. [...] The total number of measles cases in 2026 has already surpassed last year’s total, according to data posted by the CDC on Friday. At least 2,318 cases have been reported with more than five months left in the year.

title: U.S. measles cases surpass last year's total: Tracker
snippet:
The U.S. measles case count for this year has surged past last year's total and now stands at 2,295 — a level that hasn't been seen in 35 years, according to a Johns Hopkins University tracker that compiles state and local health data.

Why it matters:It's the latest sign that the virus is rebounding in areas with low vaccine coverage, threatening the United States' measles elimination status, which is due to be reviewed in November. [...] Jurisdictions including South Carolina, Utah, Texas, Florida and Arizona have the most reported cases. 
   The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 2,260 confirmed cases in its last update%20were%20outbreak%2Dassociated.) on July 16. The agency said there were 34 new outbreaks reported this year.
   The last time measles cases were higher was in 1991, when the U.S. had 9,643 cases, according to CDC data. [...] The big picture: The majority of cases are in unvaccinated people. While overall measles vaccination rates are still relatively high, public health officials say they must remain above 95% to maintain herd immunity.

By the numbers:As of Tuesday, there were nine more cases than in all of 2025, per the Johns Hopkins U.S. measles tracker.
